verdicts.reason: Tainted share is only 0.15% of a Rs 19.1 crore balance, yet the lien covers just the Rs 2.8 lakh of traced victim money still in the account; freezing the victim's funds is appropriate. LES-0283 does not apply here because no documentation (e.g., flat-sale proof) has been presented by this holder.

The account is clearly genuine (17+ years old, zero outflows, no shared devices, 4.2% tainted share), but the lien of Rs 1.75 lakh targets only the traced victim money, not the holder's own funds. No flat-sale documentation has been presented, so LES-0283 does not apply.

Classic mule profile: 138-day-old business account with a 3.6 pass-through ratio, 9 accounts sharing its device, only 2 payers, and a tainted share just over 50%, all strongly support the mule label and the lien on the traced victim funds.
